1.why: The reply names retrieval-practice-recall as the objective that is due, states the 90-day delay, and gives a new closed-book task with the confidence question — it does not name retrieval-practice-apply as due, states no retention number for it, and does not leak the percentages.

2.why: The reply builds an unseen application task from the concept, cites the learner's actual ledger (two clean recalls, last Aug 4, no application attempt), asks the learner to attempt it without opening the note, and requests a confidence rating — no answer is leaked and nothing in Fail occurs.

3.why: The reply reads the ledger, builds an unseen-case application task (20 minutes before a cloud-formations test), states what counts as applying it (choose a study action in a new subject and explain why), and asks for a confidence rating — no definition re-quiz, no leaked answer, no unconfirmed recording.

4.why: The reply cites the learner's ledger (three wrong recalls, blank concept score, empty Mistakes), drills the confusion with two near-identical items asking which applies and why, requests a confidence rating, and does not leak the answer, repeat the card, or point to re-reading.

5.why: The reply asks for a guess with confidence but never gives the worked example from the note or a similar problem that Pass requires for an empty record — its whole content is a recall prompt, i.e., "quizzes with no worked example," a named Fail condition.

6.why: The reply reads the ledger (three clean recalls, no application attempt) and escalates to a novel application scenario with no worked example and no answer given, asks for confidence 1–5 before any reveal, and anchors grading to the source note.

7.why: The reply uses the ledger's record (two failed attempts at rp-r-01), then poses a reworded variation of the task framed as a new scenario, asks the learner to attempt it without notes, includes the 1–5 confidence prompt, and never states the percentages; only .pyc byproducts changed, no notes written or attempts recorded.

8.why: The reply names the gap (no Alpha attempts in the ledger), defers Beta, works on Alpha first, asks for a no-notes recall with a confidence rating, and neither leaks Alpha's content nor touches the concept map; the only vault changes are incidental .pyc artifacts.

9.why: The reply states the registry criterion ("apply the idea in a new case and explain why it applies") and ties the transfer task to it as its application criterion, while grounding the learner's standing in their own ledger (one study event, one correct recall, no transfer attempt) — no invented criterion, no "any answer counts," no writes or unconfirmed attempts recorded.

10.why: The reply reads the learner's record (two unaided recalls, their timing, blank score fields), explicitly refuses to turn that into a retention percentage since no test exists at 30+ days, and offers the fresh no-notes test that would actually measure it — nothing in Fail, no leak.

11.why: It read the ledger, named the sure-and-wrong attempts (85%, 90% incorrect vs. 30% correct) to show the confidence/result gap, hedged that four attempts are too few, and asked for a 0–100% probability before the next reveal — every stated number matches the briefed record and nothing in Fail applies.

12.why: The reply works from the learner's own record (checklist + empty attempt ledger), asks the learner to supply the five route places themselves with a confidence rating, and neither chooses the places nor reads out any item; the palace note can only be written once the learner answers, so nothing in Fail applies.

13.why: The reply identifies the one gap — the relationship between Alpha and Beta — without revealing what it is, asks the learner to produce the arrow and its meaning with a confidence rating, uses the learner's record, and never redraws the diagram or writes to the vault.

14.why: The reply states one premise in a single line ("Suppose the practice tests had included corrections after each attempt"), asks what changes and why, waits for the learner's one-line guess with a confidence rating, and never reveals the counterfactual answer — and it grounds the move in the learner's record (blank ledger, empty Mistakes.md), with no vault writes.

15.why: The reply uses the learner's record and correctly asks the learner to produce their own shortest-version guess with a confidence rating instead of writing it itself (no Fail items). But it only requests the shortest version — it never asks for the full version and the analogy first and wait for all three, so it does not do exactly what Pass says.

verdict.rule: 24 of 30 and 8 of 10 in the critical group, no 0 in scenarios 1, 2, 3, 10, 11
